guides.d: An introduction to the main areas of Music Folder (Home, Library, Tools and Search), where to find Account, and how to try the two included examples.
guides.b: Music Folder lets you organize sheet music, chord charts, and set lists on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. This guide introduces the main areas of the app and shows you how to try the included examples before adding your own music. The first time you open the app A short welcome film plays first. Tap Get Started and the app asks What kind of music do you play? Choose Sheet Music & Scores or Chord Charts & Songs to open an example piece with a short guided tour, choose I play both to see both, or tap Skip for now to go straight to Home. You can come back to the examples at any time (see below). Home (opens the full-size image) Home is where the app opens. It shows the pieces you opened recently, your next dated set list (with Start Set to play it from the top), today's practice time and goal, and your folders. Tags you've given your pieces are at the bottom. When your library is empty, Home shows Import from Files and Browse Free Scores instead, plus Scan Sheet Music (on devices with a camera) and New Chord Chart . Add your first music walks through the first import. Library The Library holds three lists: Music : every piece in your library, as a list or a grid. Folders : groups of pieces, such as one folder per band or per concert. A piece can be in more than one folder without making a copy. Set Lists : pieces in the order you'll play them, ready to play straight through. On iPhone, tap the Library tab, then the list you want. guides.d: Import your first sheet music PDF into Music Folder from the Files app, check its title in the Add Music form, and open it in the reader.
guides.b: The quickest way to start is to import a PDF you already have, such as a score you downloaded or a part your director emailed you. Save it somewhere in the Files app first, such as iCloud Drive or Downloads, then follow these steps. Import a PDF from Files (opens the full-size image) Open the Library. On iPhone, tap the Library tab, then Music . On iPad, tap Music under Library in the sidebar (with iPadOS 17, use the Library tab as on iPhone). Tap at the top of the list. In the Add to Library menu, tap Files . Find your PDF and tap it. The Add Music form opens with the file's name as the title (marked "from file"). Change the title if you like, and add a composer. Tap to add the piece. The piece now appears in your Music list. Tap it to open it in the reader, and swipe to turn pages. Tap the back button to return to the list. Tip On a device with Apple Intelligence and iOS 26 or later, the form can also fill in a title, composer, key, tempo or time signature printed on the first page. Anything it can't read stays blank, so check the details before you save. If your library is still empty, Home shows an Import from Files button that does the same thing. When you import a single piece from there, it opens in the reader as soon as you save it. Add several files at once In the Files picker, tap Select , choose the PDFs you want, then tap Open . Instead of the Add Music form, you'll see a list titled Add 3 Pieces (or however many you picked). Check the titles, choose a folder for them if you like, then tap . guides.d: What the free version of Music Folder includes, its limits of 15 pieces, 5 sections and 1 folder, what Premium adds, the free trial, and earlier purchases.
guides.b: Music Folder is free to use with a small library, and the free version has no time limit. Premium removes the limits on pieces, sections and folders, and adds the practice tools, chord chart transposition, collaboration and Planning Center. What's free The free version covers reading and organizing a small library: Up to 15 pieces , 5 sections (counted across your whole library) and 1 folder Set lists, including playing them straight through The reader, Performance Mode, Two-Page View and Bluetooth page turners Chord charts: writing, importing and reading them Annotation with Apple Pencil, annotation layers, and notes on each piece Recordings attached to your pieces Free sheet music from the built-in catalog Backups and iCloud sync Sending a one-time copy of a piece, folder or set list to someone else The two example pieces in Account › Support › Examples don't count toward the limits, and Premium tools such as Transpose work in them for free. What Premium adds Unlimited music, sections and folders The metronome, the tuner, reference tones and drones, and the 88-key piano Transposing a chord chart and setting a capo (reading a chart in its written key is free) Face Gesture page turning on devices that support it (setting it up and trying it are free) Collaboration on folders and set lists Planning Center Services (you also need a Planning Center Services account) Collaboration is Premium for everyone taking part: the person who shares a folder or set list and each person who joins it. guides.b: On a Mac with Apple silicon, Music Folder runs as its iPad app. With iCloud sync, your library, set lists and annotations are the same as on your iPhone or iPad, and on the Mac you also get a menu bar, keyboard shortcuts and drag and drop from the Finder. Install and sign in On your Mac, open the App Store and search for Music Folder. It's listed with the iPhone and iPad apps. Install it with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone or iPad. Open the app. If iCloud is on for your Mac, your library syncs in the same way it does on your other devices (see Sync with iCloud ). Premium carries over: a subscription or Lifetime purchase made with the same Apple Account works on the Mac too. If it doesn't show, open Account, tap Upgrade to Premium , then Restore Purchases . The window The window works like an iPad screen. You can resize it freely or use full screen, and the layout adapts to the space: a wide window uses the iPad layout, while a narrow one switches to the iPhone-style tab bar. The window can't be made narrower than an iPhone screen. In a wide window, the reader can show two pages side by side. Open a piece, then choose ⋯ › Page Display & Layout › Two-Page View . Add PDFs from the Finder Drag one or more PDFs from the Finder onto the Music list. Drop them on a folder's list instead to add them to that folder. guides.b: You can turn pages without taking your hands off your instrument in two ways: with a Bluetooth page turner pedal, or with Face Gestures, which turn the page when you hold a head turn, a wink or a mouth movement. Both work in every reader, including set lists and Planning Center plans, and turns made either way follow your Half-Page Turns and Page Links settings. Connect a Bluetooth page turner A Bluetooth page turner pedal (AirTurn, PageFlip and Donner make common ones) connects to your device as a keyboard, so there's nothing to set up in the app. Pair the pedal in the Settings app under Bluetooth, following its maker's instructions. Set the pedal to a mode that sends the arrow keys or Page Up and Page Down. A mode that sends Space and Enter works too. Open a piece and press the pedal. Pedals set to a media or volume mode aren't supported. If your pedal has those modes, switch it to an arrow key or Page Up/Down mode. Test your pedal Go to Account › Preferences › Page Turner . Press each pedal. The screen shows the key the pedal sends and what it does in a reader, such as "Right Arrow → Next Page". Nothing turns on this screen. (opens the full-size image) If you see "Not a page-turn key", the pedal is in a mode the app doesn't use. Change the pedal's mode and press it again. If the pedals turn the wrong way, turn on Swap Forward and Back on the same screen. The setting also swaps the arrow keys on a keyboard. guides.d: Use Performance Mode on stage: the toolbars hide, taps and pedals only turn pages, and nothing on the page can be changed by accident until you leave.
guides.b: Performance Mode is the reader for playing on stage or in a service. The toolbars and status bar disappear, the page gets the whole screen, and a touch on the page can only turn it, so nothing opens, zooms or gets marked up by accident in the middle of a piece. (opens the full-size image) Start Performance Mode In any reader: choose ⋯ › Performance Mode . It's the first item in the menu. From a set list: tap Perform Set . The set list starts from its first item in Performance Mode. Tapping an item in the list opens it in the regular reader instead. From the toolbar: if you play this way often, add the Performance Mode button to the toolbar (see The reader at a glance ). Performance Mode lasts until you leave it, through every piece of a set list or Planning Center plan, and the reader opens normally the next time. Turn pages in Performance Mode Tap the right two thirds of the page to go forward, and the left third to go back. Swipe left or up for the next page, and right or down for the previous one. Pedals, keyboards and Face Gestures turn pages as usual. Half-Page Turns and Page Links keep working: with Half-Page Turns on, each turn moves half a page, and tapping a link's marker still jumps. Pinching doesn't zoom unless you turn on Allow Pinch to Zoom in the settings below. Use tools while you perform A small capsule in the top-right corner holds the tools you've allowed, which by default are Notes, Metronome and Audio Playback. Word documents and notation files (MusicXML, MuseScore, Sibelius, Finale, Dorico) can't be imported. Export or print them to PDF from the app that made them, then import the PDF. Chord chart text files (.cho, .chordpro, .chopro, .pro, .crd and .txt) become chord charts, not PDFs. See Create a chord chart . On Mac, the same menu items are called Import from Files , Import from Photos and Import Folder . Check the free version's limit The free version holds up to 15 pieces and 5 sections in your library. When you reach the limit, adding more opens the Premium screen, headed Keep adding to your library , instead of the import. Adding sections past the fifth opens it headed Unlock Unlimited Sections .
